assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: gap:interrupt.

## This settles the column's most load-bearing UNVERIFIED item

The format-spec's own corpus research (`muse-format-spec.md` §12, `muse-capabilities.md`) found `terminal:"cancelled"` only inside SUBAGENT run streams, with internal-sounding reasons ("cancelled during model step", "...end-of-turn reminder wait", "...tool result reconciliation") that read as programmatic cancellation, not a confirmed human ESC. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go:342-360` (parseRunTerminal) therefore deliberately leaves `ev.IsUserInterrupt` false for every `cancelled` terminal, with a comment saying so and citing the same caveat.

I live-drove this today (never inside the repo): `tmux new-session -d -s museescprobe -c <scratch>/cwd "muse --trust-workspace"`, waited for `ready`, sent "Use your bash/execute tool to run the shell command: sleep 60 ; echo DONE_SLEEPING . Then reply with the word FINISHED.", waited ~5s until the pane showed `◈ Thinking (5s · esc to interrupt)` mid-tool-dispatch, then `tmux send-keys Escape`. The pane immediately showed `◆ Ran command · ... · ⋘ · cancelled · 0.3s` and `◆ Interrupted · Report issues with /feedback`.

On disk, the newly-minted TOP-LEVEL session `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/01a09eeb-5ee1-76c1-baf2-1db7316588d3/session.jsonl` (NOT a `subagent/` file — confirmed by the run's own `owner`: `{"requester_kind":"main","owner_type":"main_root"}` on the `goal_usage_attribution` event for this same run_id) recorded:
```
run.started  run_id=5252a27d prompt="Use your bash/execute tool to run the shell command: sleep 60 ; echo DONE_SLEEPING ..."
...task cancelled: {"kind":"cancelled","reason":"cancelled by tool cancellation"}
...reminder.cleanup_effect.started: {"mode":"main_run_cancelled", ...}
run.terminal run_id=5252a27d {"terminal":"cancelled","reason":"cancelled after tool result reconciliation","turn_duration_ms":9738,"time_to_first_token_ms":8246}
run.started  run_id=102813a8 prompt="Reply with exactly the word: RECOVERED"
run.terminal run_id=102813a8 {"terminal":"completed","reason":null,...}
```
A second, clean prompt right after ("Reply with exactly the word: RECOVERED") produced a normal `started→...→terminal:completed` arc with a NEW run_id — no stuck state, no leftover flag.

Three things this proves:
1. **A genuine human ESC keypress on the TOP-LEVEL (main-root) session DOES produce `terminal:"cancelled"`**, using the exact same `reason` vocabulary the corpus had previously only seen on subagent streams (`"cancelled after tool result reconciliation"` verbatim). This settles the format-spec's §12 UNVERIFIED item for the main-session case: it is real, and it is what a human ESC produces.
2. The `reason` string describes the PIPELINE STAGE the cancellation landed in (model step / eot-wait / tool-result reconciliation), not the actor — muse's own `TurnInterruptParams`/`TurnInterruptResult` wire schema (`scratchpad/muse-schema/msp.schema.json`, dumped offline via `muse schema generate-json-schema`) confirms this structurally: `turn/interrupt` is documented as "the '**user pressed stop**' gesture, on the runtime's priority lane", and its result folds into `turn/completed` with terminal `'cancelled'` — i.e. `cancelled` is BY PROTOCOL DESIGN the client-stop-gesture terminal state for a top-level run. There is no separate `retract`/`actor` field surfaced into `session.jsonl` distinguishing WHO issued the client gesture — confirmed by a full-text scan of the transcript for `interrupt`/`commandId`/`retract` (0 protocol-level hits; the 6 literal "interrupt" substring hits are all inside reminder-subagent SYSTEM PROMPT boilerplate, e.g. "uninterrupted verification phase").
3. **The canonical scenario arc does not need `IsUserInterrupt` at all for muse.** `parseRunTerminal` sets `ev.EventType="turn_done"` uniformly for `completed` AND `cancelled` ("every one of them is the run's own terminal record, so the turn objectively ended", parser.go:316-320). `state_classifier.go`'s `agent_done` rule (`tierAgentDone`, fires on `IsAgentDone()`) is checked BEFORE the `user_interrupt` rule in the ordered ladder (`ClassifyStateTiered` returns on first match, ~line 366) and its `classifyAgentDone` decide-fn routes turn_done → ready (or waiting/error) with zero dependency on `LastWasUserInterrupt`. So muse's `ready→working→ready` arc, no-stuck-in-working, and clean-reset-on-next-prompt (the scenario's 4 acceptance bullets) are ALL already produced by shipped code — confirmed by architecture read AND by the live probe above (both turns landed exactly as classified). Nothing about `IsUserInterrupt` changes this arc; claudecode needs that flag because it has NO OTHER completion signal on interrupt, muse does not share that architecture.

**Caveat, not a bug** (per the assess rubric — canonical arc met, narrow detail gappy): none of the machine-checked spec phases in ANY agent's `user-esc-interrupt` cell (including claudecode's own, the reference for this scenario) assert the classifier's internal REASON string — only the STATE. Since the state arc is fully and correctly produced, `daemon_capability=full` is honest. But `IsUserInterrupt`/`LastWasUserInterrupt` staying permanently false for muse means the daemon can never LABEL a transition as interrupt-caused (vs. ordinary completion) for anything that reads the reason/tier metadata (logs, future UI surfacing, `decided_by_rule` in richer diagnostics). Given finding #1 above, that caution is now empirically outdated for the main-session case and is worth revisiting — see caveats. This is exactly the kind of adapter change the dispatcher, not this assess pass, should schedule.

## Driver pillar

`replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh:670` stubs `interrupt) not_implemented interrupt ;;` and `DRIVE_ELICITS` (line 167) does not list `interrupt`. This IS live-portable, trivially: my manual probe's interrupt step was exactly `tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION" Escape` (verified working, twice — once mid-probe, once implicitly via the settle wait), the same primitive claudecode's own `step_interrupt()` (`replaydata/agents/claudecode/driver-interactive.sh:469-477`) already uses. `record` ports this before driving, per the standard driver-gap flow.
caveats: RECOMMENDED ADAPTER FOLLOW-UP (not implemented here, per task scope): core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go's parseRunTerminal (terminalCancelled case, ~line 342-360) could now set ev.IsUserInterrupt=true for a cancelled terminal on the session's OWN top-level run (not a subagent's), citing this cell's live evidence. The discriminator should NOT be 'any cancelled terminal' indiscriminately: the corpus's subagent-stream cancelled examples remain unconfirmed as human-vs-parent-cancelled, and a subagent's own run cancellation may be orchestrator-initiated rather than a literal ESC. Scoping the flag to main-root runs (the adapter already threads subagent-vs-main context structurally, since subagent transcripts live under a distinguishable subagent/<child>/ path and become separate irrlicht sessions) avoids a false positive on that ambiguous case. This is a real, live-evidenced fix opportunity, not a blocking defect — flagging for the dispatcher to schedule, not implementing it in this assess pass.

The interrupted run in my probe still showed a completed model call (reasoning_committed + model_completed) BEFORE the tool cancellation landed — the interrupt fired mid-tool-execution, not mid-model-stream. I did not separately test an ESC during the 'Thinking' phase before any tool call was proposed; the scenario's acceptance criteria ('before the agent emits a turn-done marker') is satisfied either way (turn_duration_ms=9738 for a `sleep 60` command that cannot have completed naturally), but a spec asserting a SPECIFIC interrupt-timing shape (e.g. no tool call at all) would need a different recipe.

Vacuous-pass guard: the recipe's interrupted turn MUST run an operation that provably cannot complete naturally within the phase's max_delay_ms bound (here: a `sleep 45` shell command via the bash tool, bounded well under its own floor) — NOT a 'long essay' prompt as claudecode's sibling recipe uses. Because muse's agent_done classifier tier treats cancelled and natural completion identically, a long-essay-style recipe would let this cell pass even if the interrupt driver step were a silent no-op and the model simply finished on its own. This is a genuine adapter-specific deviation from the claudecode template, made necessary by muse's different (more robust) turn-boundary architecture.

Live-verified today on muse 1.2.1 with the `meta` provider (model muse-spark-1.3-contributor); not yet run through an actual irrlichd + websocket pipeline (that is record's job) — this assessment is grounded in the raw muse transcript plus a code read of the daemon's parser/classifier, both matched line-for-line against the corpus, not a live daemon observation.

sources.note: Live ESC-probe transcript (today, this assess pass): run_id 5252a27d started with prompt 'sleep 60 ...', tmux Escape sent at ~+6s while pane showed 'Thinking (5s . esc to interrupt)', run.terminal landed {"terminal":"cancelled","reason":"cancelled after tool result reconciliation","turn_duration_ms":9738}; owner.requester_kind="main"/owner_type="main_root" on the same run_id's goal_usage_attribution event confirms this is the TOP-LEVEL session's own run, not a subagent. A second prompt (run_id 102813a8) completed cleanly right after: {"terminal":"completed","reason":null}.

Lines ~316-360 (parseRunTerminal): EventType="turn_done" set uniformly for completed/cancelled/failed; IsUserInterrupt deliberately left false for `cancelled`, with the pre-existing UNVERIFIED comment this assess pass resolves for the main-session case.

stateRules is an ordered ladder (ClassifyStateTiered, ~line 366, returns on first `when` match). The agent_done rule (tierAgentDone, ~line 290-303, fires on IsAgentDone()) precedes the user_interrupt rule (~line 305-323) in that list, so classifyAgentDone (turn_done -> ready, absent SessionError/waiting-cue) decides muse's cancelled-terminal case without ever consulting LastWasUserInterrupt.

TurnInterruptParams/TurnInterruptResult (dumped via `muse schema generate-json-schema`, offline, exact for this binary): `turn/interrupt` is documented as the "'user pressed stop' gesture, on the runtime's priority lane"; its result folds into `turn/completed` with terminal 'cancelled' -- protocol-level confirmation that `cancelled` on a top-level run is the client-stop-gesture terminal state.
Line 167 (DRIVE_ELICITS, does not list 'interrupt') and line 670 (`interrupt) not_implemented interrupt ;;`) -- the driver-pillar gap; record ports the Escape-key primitive before driving.
Template/precedent read per the assess SKILL.md's instruction; muse's spec deliberately diverges from claudecode's 'long essay' recipe shape for the vacuous-pass reason cited in caveats.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH, v1.2.1 (muse --version >= 1.2.1 per replaydata/agents/muse/metadata.json)
muse auth complete: 'muse login' (Meta account) or META_API_KEY exported -- auth is set up out-of-band, the rig's precheck delegates it to the user
tmux available -- the interactive driver runs muse in a tmux REPL so it stays alive across the turn (bare `muse` with no subcommand starts the interactive TUI)
irrlichd is recording -- either run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record

the interrupt step must be ported into driver-interactive.sh before this cell can record (driver_capability=gap:interrupt); port target is `tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION" Escape`, live-confirmed working against muse 1.2.1's TUI
setup: The interactive driver (driver-interactive.sh) creates a fresh empty cwd under <staging>/cwd/ and launches `muse --trust-workspace` in a tmux session there, then sleeps 1s before the first send
--trust-workspace is REQUIRED: every staging cwd is brand-new, so muse's 'Do you trust this workspace?' modal fires on every run and silently eats the first prompt without it

The first turn asks muse to run a real `sleep 45` shell command via its bash/execute tool -- deliberately un-completable within the phase's timing bound, so the recording cannot pass vacuously even if the interrupt step silently no-ops (see caveats)
The driver sleeps 6s after sending the first prompt (matching the live probe's observed timing: the tool call is dispatched and 'esc to interrupt' is showing by ~5s) before sending Escape
A second, short prompt right after the interrupt settles proves the parser resets cleanly (process step 6 of the scenario: 'the next user prompt drives a clean ready -> working -> ready arc')

script.text: Use your bash/execute tool to run the shell command: sleep 45 ; echo DONE_SLEEPING . Then reply with the word FINISHED.
Reply with exactly the word: RECOVERED

verify: events.jsonl mints the session in ready shortly after muse's TUI finishes launching (single-birth; session id from the session directory basename == stream.id)
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered event binding the muse-bin PID to the session
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to working when the first (sleep 45) prompt lands

events.jsonl contains a state_transition to ready WELL BEFORE 45s have elapsed since that working transition -- the only way this can happen is a genuine interrupt, since the shell command physically cannot finish that fast
no state_transition to error or waiting occurs for the interrupted turn
events.jsonl contains a second state_transition to working for the follow-up prompt, then back to ready on normal completion -- proving the parser did not stick in any interrupt-related state
final session state is ready before exit_clean tears the REPL down
